# Seyf

> Seyf is a savings app for Mexico built fully on Stellar mainnet. Users sign in with an email (Pollar co-signed wallet: no seed phrase, no extension, no XLM needed), save USDC in a DeFindex vault that earns real Blend yield, and get tomorrow's yield advanced today by our own Soroban contract, `seyf_advance`, without touching their principal. Built for HackMeridian 2026 (Category: Scale · Track: Stellar Composed).

Key facts for reviewers:

- Network: Stellar mainnet (Protocol 29). Every step of the user journey has a mainnet transaction, listed below.
- Our Soroban contract `seyf_advance`: `CCZ77VBEZZIRBK3Z7RO4W227764G76ILXKO664R622FOSJTE7BX4CWXH` (wasm hash `64ae06cb3e50eb304b2eb8b7dc2be9f9271432b04d77b0f2a9eeded899e9bdfa`, same as testnet and the CI build).
- Savings vault: DeFindex "Meru" USDC vault `CCA2ZJP5BVRXYTQH4FAGHCAUMRYCXVC4CRYC2NXHWMR7TIVX36U7F5HR`, strategy "USDC Autocompound Blend Fixed" `CDB2WMKQQNVZMEBY7Q7GZ5C7E7IAFSNMZ7GGVD6WKTCEWK7XOIAVZSAP`.
- Asset: Circle USDC `GA5ZSEJYB37JRC5AVCIA5MOP4RHTM335X2KGX3IHOJAPP5RE34K4KZVN` (SAC `CCW67TSZV3SSS2HXMBQ5JFGCKJNXKZM7UQUWUZPUTHXSTZLEO7SJMI75`).
- Try it: the allowlist is off, so any account can open an advance at https://www.seyf.app/app. Beta caps are 1 USDC per user and 2 USDC in total, because the contract is not audited yet.
- Composed from: Pollar (wallet), DeFindex (vault), Blend (yield), Circle USDC, plus our own contract, sponsor and keeper.

## How the yield advance works

- Advance: `A = floor(V × apy_bps × term_days / (10000 × 365))`, capped by LTV (`max_advance_bps`), per user and globally. `min_advance` protects the user from slippage.
- `open_advance(user, shares, term_days, min_advance)` locks the user's vault shares in the contract (they keep earning in Blend) and pays `A` in USDC from the contract's own treasury, never from the vault or the user's principal.
- `repay(user)`: the user returns `A` and every share unlocks at once, even while the contract is paused.
- `settle(user)` is permissionless: once `V_now ≥ V_open + A`, the contract withdraws only `ceil(A × shares / V_now)` shares back to the treasury and returns the rest (the full principal). Our keeper (GitHub Actions) calls it every 10 minutes.
- `pause` only blocks new advances. There is no upgrade entry point; admin handover is two-step (`propose_admin` / `accept_admin`).
- 17 contract tests (`cd soroban && cargo test`), `soroban-sdk` 29.0.1.

## Architecture

- Frontend: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind v4. UI in Mexican Spanish, amounts shown in MXN.
- Wallet: Pollar co-signed Stellar account (Turnkey 2-of-2); a passkey or email recovers it. Session via SEP-10 Web Auth at `https://www.seyf.app/api/auth/sep10`.
- Fees: our sponsor pays reserves and wraps every transaction in a fee-bump with a capped resource fee. The server builds XDR but never holds user funds; the user signs every transaction.
- RPC: `https://mainnet.sorobanrpc.com` (gateway.fm as fallback).
- SEP-1 info file: https://www.seyf.app/.well-known/stellar.toml (SEP-10 signing key, web-auth endpoint and the accounts we control).

## Optional

- Problem: even after Mexico's 2020 pension reform, a middle-income worker is projected to retire on about 45% of their salary (experts recommend 70%+), and fewer than 3 in 100 savers save voluntarily for retirement. Target users: Mexican millennials aged 30–45, the first generation fully dependent on their Afore.
- Team history: testnet prototype built at Hack+Alebrije (Mexico City, March 2026, 2nd place); core shipped to Stellar mainnet during HackMeridian (Oct 25–26, 2026).
- Roadmap: incorporate in Mexico to integrate regulated anchors (SPEI peso on/off-ramps), Etherfuse Stablebonds (CETES, Tesouro, US Treasuries, Gilts, EU bonds) as savings options, audit via SCF Audit Bank before raising caps.
